                    ### Question
                    Which of the following drugs is used to treat both diabetes mellitus and diabetes insipidus

                    ### Options
                    opa. Chlorpropamide
opb. Glibenclamide
opc. Glicazide
opd. Glipizide

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Chlorpropamide is unique among the options as it is used to treat both diabetes mellitus and diabetes insipidus. It increases insulin secretion to manage diabetes mellitus and enhances ADH effect in the kidney to reduce urine output in diabetes insipidus. Other drugs like Glibenclamide, Glicazide, and Glipizide are effective in diabetes mellitus but lack action on ADH pathways, making them ineffective for diabetes insipidus.
